To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MCD and median/MAD are robust for both masking and swamping, and that Mahalanobis standardization is competitive with respect to swamping robustness.

the Mahalanobiss distance outlyingness function, using MCD for location and scatter estimation, is the best choice for robust outlier detection in multivariate settings, followed by Mahalanobis-spatial, using MCD standardization.

Mahalanobis outlyingness with minimum covariance determinant location and scatter estimations, projection outlyingness, and Mahalanobis-spatial outlyingness with standardization using MCD are all highly robust to masking and swamping.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the robustness of nonparametric outlier detection methods, with a particular focus on the finite-sample robustness properties of the Mahalanobisspatial and Mahalanobis-distance outlyingness functions, which are widely used for outlier detection in high-dimensional data sets.
the robustness of three important outlyingness measures in the multivariate setting, with a view to providing guidance for practitioners in their use.
the development of nonparametric robustness measures for outlier identification in multivariate data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three nonparametric outlyingness functions considered here, when combined with appropriate robust location and scatter estimations, are all highly robust with respect to masking and swamping.
MCD is the best all-around nonparametric outlier identifier for multivariate data, and is the recommended choice for general use.

, in the multivariate data context, Mahalanobos distance outlyingness with location and scatter estimates obtained by the minimum covariance determinant estimator is the leading contender for a general-purpose robust nonparametric outlier identifier, and that Mahalanobis outlyingness with standardization by MCD standardization, although not as good, is also a strong contender.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the multivariate data case, MCD location and scatter estimations are the most desirable, followed by the MAD median univariate estimators, and the Mahalanobics spatial outlyingness function with MCD standardizations.

MCD-based Mahalanobis outlyingness and projection outlyingness are recommended for outlier detection in multivariate data, with Mahalanobis and projection outlying functions having the same masking and swamping finite-sample breakdown points.

, when one is concerned primarily with masking robustness, then Mahalanobis outlyingness is the best choice, while when swamping robust is of primary interest, then Mahalanbois spatial outlying is the best choice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the three outlyingness functions considered, MCD location and scatter estimation, with or without spatial standardization, is the most robust choice, with respect to both masking and swamping, for identifying outlying data in multivariate data settings.
the Mahalanobís distance outlyingness with minimum covariance determinant (or minimum volume ellipsoid) estimators is a good choice for multivariate outlier detection.

the MCD location/scatter and projection median/MAD estimators can be recommended as robust alternatives to the more popular robust location/scatter estimators, the affine equivariant S-estimators and minimum covariance determinant (MCV) location/scatter estimator, in outlier detection applications where masking and swamping error control is important.
